title: Four enablement reviews
intro:
*Five minutes. Commit before you look.*

Four People Ops teams documented the decision to switch on an AI feature that arrived in their HCM's quarterly release. All four produced something.

**One of them survives an auditor reading it a year later.** Find it — and notice what the other three did instead.

artifacts.label: Review A
artifacts.body: "Capability: résumé-ranking in the internal mobility module. Population: all 3,100 employees — the feature cannot be scoped to a subset, confirmed in config, so no pilot is available and we have said so. Reads: job history, skills, performance rating (config screen shows rating is included; we have disabled that field). Writes: nothing to the record; ranking is display-only. Gate: Dana Okonkwo reviews every shortlist before it reaches a hiring manager, and has declined four so far. Logs: 90-day retention, exportable as CSV, inputs NOT captured — vendor confirmed by email, ticket #44120, and we have asked for input logging in the renewal. Rollback: performed in sandbox by Dana, 11 minutes. 3am failure: Dana, and she does have the admin role. Accountable: Dana Okonkwo. Open: whether ranking order is reproducible — unknown, owner Dana, due 30 September."

artifacts.label: Review B
artifacts.body: "Capability: résumé-ranking in the internal mobility module. This feature was reviewed against our AI Acceptable Use Policy and found compliant. The vendor is SOC 2 Type II certified and their AI is built on an enterprise-grade foundation model with no training on customer data. The HRIS steering group approved enablement at its 14 April meeting (minutes attached). Human oversight is maintained throughout — hiring managers make all final decisions. Data is encrypted in transit and at rest. The vendor's AI governance whitepaper is attached for reference. Risk rating: Low."

artifacts.label: Review C
artifacts.body: "Capability: résumé-ranking in the internal mobility module. Population: piloting with the 240-person Commercial function — they volunteered and their director is keen. Reads: job history and skills. Writes: display-only. Gate: hiring managers see the ranking alongside the full applicant list. Logs: 90 days, exportable. Rollback: documented in the runbook, section 4.2. Baseline: we'll pull internal-mobility application volumes and time-to-shortlist after the first month so we can see the trend. Accountable: People Technology team. Decision point: end of pilot, and if it goes well we extend to the whole company in Q1."

artifacts.label: Review D
artifacts.body: "Capability: résumé-ranking in the internal mobility module. We ran a bias assessment: 400 historical applications re-scored, pass-through rates compared by gender and ethnicity, four-fifths rule satisfied on both. Population: all employees. Reads: job history, skills, performance rating. Writes: display-only. Gate: hiring managers. Logs: retained per vendor default. Rollback: support ticket to vendor, they estimate 24-48 hours. Accountable: Head of People Technology. We are comfortable proceeding on the strength of the bias testing, which is more diligence than any peer we spoke to had done."

reasoning:
**A survives, and the reason it survives is the thing that looks like weakness.** It contains an unknown, a limitation, and a named gap — inputs are not logged, ranking reproducibility is unresolved, and the capability cannot be scoped so there is no pilot. Every one of those is stated, sourced, and owned with a date. An auditor reading A a year later learns what was decided, on what evidence, by whom, and what was still open. That is what the document is for.

Note the specific tells of a real answer. **Citations rather than assurances**: "config screen shows rating is included," "vendor confirmed by email, ticket #44120." **A gate with evidence it functions** — Dana has declined four, which is the only proof a gate is real. **A rollback that was performed**, with a time. And the 3am question actually checked, including the permission, which is the question Lesson 2 says finds the most real problems.

**B is the most common document in this category and it is not a review at all — it is a compliance narrative.** Every sentence is true and not one answers a question about this capability. SOC 2 is an audit of the vendor's controls, not of what the feature does to your population. "Human oversight is maintained throughout" is the reassurance Lesson 2 names specifically: no person, no step, no authority to refuse. "Hiring managers make all final decisions" is the sentence that will not survive being read aloud, because the ranking shapes which candidates a manager ever sees. And **"Risk rating: Low" is a conclusion with no derivation** — the one thing an auditor will circle.

**C is well-intentioned and fails on three specific things**, which makes it the useful distractor. The pilot population **volunteered and their director is keen** — Lesson 4's surprising criterion, and it means the result predicts nothing about the other 2,860 people. The baseline is being taken **after the first month**, which Module 2 says is not a baseline; the before is now permanently unobservable. The rollback is **documented in the runbook**, which is exactly the distinction Module 2 draws: documented is not performed. And accountability is assigned to a **team**, which cannot sign anything. Then the last clause gives the game away: *if it goes well we extend* — the decision has two permitted outcomes, not three, which makes it a rollout with a preamble.

**D is the interesting one, because the diligence is real and aimed at the wrong layer.** Re-scoring 400 historical applications and comparing pass-through rates by group is genuine, non-trivial work and more than most teams do. It is also an answer to a question nobody in this module asked. **Bias testing tells you about the model's outputs; it tells you nothing about logs, rollback, provenance, the gate, or who is accountable at 3am** — and D's answers to those are "per vendor default," "support ticket, 24-48 hours," and a job title. A capability you cannot switch off inside two days is not one you control, however fair its scoring. The closing sentence is the real failure: **"more diligence than any peer" is a peer comparison, not evidence**, and it is precisely the reasoning Module 1 warned about.

The transferable test: **read the document as someone who wants to blame you.** Which sentences would you have to defend, and which ones would you have to admit you cannot support? A has four sentences it could not support and says so first. B, C and D each have several and do not.
